s1.syndrome_frame: Acute neck pain with stiffness and fever
salient_findings: Firm swelling in the posterior triangle of the left neck
key_facts: CT and MRI findings: poorly defined collection and intramuscular abscess in the left paraspinal musculature

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute neck pain with stiffness and fever
salient_findings: Firm swelling in the posterior triangle of the left neck
key_facts: CT and MRI findings: poorly defined collection and intramuscular abscess in the left paraspinal musculature

shortlist.label: Fusobacterium necrophorum infection
shortlist.why_kept: Microbiological culture confirmed F necrophorum infection, consistent with patient's symptoms and imaging findings

shortlist.label: Lemierre's syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms of neck pain, stiffness, and fever, along with F necrophorum infection, are consistent with Lemierre's syndrome

shortlist.label: Parapharyngeal abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging studies showed an intramuscular abscess in the left paraspinal musculature, which could be related to a parapharyngeal abscess

shortlist.label: Staphylococcal abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated white blood cell count and C-reactive protein suggest a bacterial infection, and Staphylococcal abscess is a possible cause of the patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Pyomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging findings of an intramuscular abscess and the patient's symptoms of neck pain and stiffness are consistent with pyomyositis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of left-sided neck pain, neck stiffness, headache, and pyrexia, combined with the laboratory confirmation of F necrophorum infection and imaging findings of an intramuscular abscess, strongly supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Lemierre's syndrome
rejected.why: Lemierre's syndrome typically involves septic thrombophlebitis of the internal jugular vein and distant septic emboli, which are not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Parapharyngeal abscess
rejected.why: The location of the abscess in the left paraspinal musculature, as shown on CT and MRI, does not correspond to the typical location of a parapharyngeal abscess.

rejected.label: Staphylococcal abscess
rejected.why: The microbiological culture identified F necrophorum, not Staphylococcus, as the causative organism.

rejected.label: Pyomyositis
rejected.why: While pyomyositis is a muscle infection that could present similarly, the specific identification of F necrophorum infection makes it a more precise diagnosis in this case.

gold: Pyomyositis of the levator scapulae muscle caused by Fusobacterium necrophorum
